title: Narrow USDA's mission to focus on agriculture
proposal: The text recommends that Congress limit the Agriculture Department's role so its main focus is agriculture, and offers a model mission statement centered on research, safety and removing trade and regulatory barriers.
quote: Congress must limit the USDA’s role. A proper mission would clarify that the department’s primary focus is on agriculture

title: Withdraw from U.N. sustainable-development efforts on food
proposal: The text recommends removing the U.S. from any association with U.N. and other efforts to push sustainable-development plans tied to food production.
quote: Remove the U.S. from any association with U.N. and other efforts to push sustainable-development schemes connected to food production.

title: Issue an executive order setting pro-production farm principles
proposal: The text recommends announcing the administration's agriculture principles in an executive order and removing references to "transforming the food system" from USDA websites and materials.
quote: a new Administration should announce its principles through an executive order, the USDA should remove all references

title: Review USDA efforts that push preferred farming practices
proposal: The text recommends that USDA carefully review programs that it says improperly push the department's preferred farming practices, such as organic or "climate-smart" methods, onto farmers.
quote: The USDA should also carefully review existing efforts that involve inappropriately imposing its preferred agricultural practices onto farmers.

title: Stop using USDA's discretionary Commodity Credit Corporation spending power
proposal: The text recommends that the Agriculture Secretary not use the Commodity Credit Corporation's section 5 discretionary authority, which it calls a "slush fund."
quote: Refrain from using section 5 discretionary authority. The USDA can address this abuse on its own

title: Repeal the Agriculture Secretary's CCC discretionary authority
proposal: The text recommends that Congress repeal the Secretary's discretionary spending authority under section 5 of the CCC Charter Act, or at least require prior congressional approval.
quote: Ideally, Congress would repeal the Secretary’s discretionary authority under section 5 of the Charter Act.

title: Limit CCC spending to genuine, temporary farm emergencies
proposal: At a minimum, the text recommends amending the law so CCC money only helps farmers and ranchers with real, temporary emergencies, and allowing court challenges to improper use.
quote: Prohibit the CCC from being used to assist parties beyond farmers and ranchers.

title: Repeal the federal sugar program
proposal: The text recommends legislation to repeal the federal sugar program, which it says limits supply and raises prices.
quote: Repeal the federal sugar program. The federal government should not be in the central planning business

title: Repeal the ARC and PLC farm subsidy programs
proposal: The text recommends, ideally, repealing the Agriculture Risk Coverage and Price Loss Coverage programs, noting farmers can already buy federal crop insurance.
quote: Ideally, repeal the ARC and PLC programs. Farmers eligible to participate in ARC or PLC

title: Stop paying farmers twice for the same losses
proposal: The text recommends barring farmers from getting an ARC or PLC payment in the same year they receive a crop insurance payout.
quote: Congress should prohibit this duplication by prohibiting farmers from receiving an ARC or PLC payment the same year they receive a crop insurance indemnity.

title: Cut taxpayer share of crop insurance premiums to 50% or less
proposal: The text recommends reducing the taxpayer-paid share of crop insurance premiums from about 60 percent to no more than 50 percent.
quote: At a minimum, taxpayers should not pay more than 50 percent of the premium.

title: Demand an open farm bill process
proposal: The text recommends that the White House and USDA insist the farm bill be written in an open process with time for amendments, including outside the Agriculture Committees.
quote: The White House and the USDA should make it very clear that the farm bill process, including reform of farm subsidies, must be

title: Split farm programs from food stamps in the farm bill
proposal: The text recommends considering agricultural programs in separate legislation from food stamps and nutrition programs, on different renewal timelines.
quote: Separate the agricultural provisions of the farm bill from the nutrition provisions.

title: Move food stamps and other nutrition programs to HHS
proposal: The text recommends moving USDA's food and nutrition programs, such as SNAP and WIC, to the Department of Health and Human Services, which would eliminate USDA's Food and Nutrition Service.
quote: Move the USDA food and nutrition programs to the Department of Health and Human Services.

title: Restore stricter SNAP work requirements
proposal: The text recommends bringing back stricter work requirements for adults without dependents in SNAP, including limits on state waivers like the Trump-era rule that a court blocked.
quote: Re-implement work requirements. The statutory language covering food stamps allows states to waive work requirements

title: Clarify state options for SNAP's general work requirement
proposal: The text recommends new rules clarifying how states can apply SNAP's general work requirement, including requiring states to offer job training slots to those who ask.
quote: FNS should implement better regulation to clarify options for states to implement the general work requirement

title: Close the broad-based categorical eligibility path into SNAP
proposal: The text recommends reforming "broad-based categorical eligibility," which it says lets people bypass SNAP income and asset limits by receiving minimal benefits from other programs.
quote: Reform broad-based categorical eligibility. Federal law permits states to enroll individuals in food stamps if they receive a benefit from another program

title: Re-evaluate the 2021 increase in SNAP benefits
proposal: The text recommends re-evaluating the 2021 Thrifty Food Plan update, which raised food stamp benefits by at least 23 percent.
quote: Re-evaluate the Thrifty Food Plan. In a dramatic overreach, the Biden Administration unilaterally increased food stamp benefits

title: Close the SNAP 'heat-and-eat' loophole
proposal: The text recommends ending the practice of states giving small energy aid payments so households qualify for a larger SNAP utility deduction and bigger benefits.
quote: Eliminate the heat-and-eat loophole. States can artificially boost a household’s food stamp benefit

title: Reform WIC infant formula contracts to avoid monopolies
proposal: The text recommends reforming the state WIC system where one infant formula brand wins each state contract, so that the rules do not create monopolies.
quote: it is vital that regulation for these competitive bidding contracts does not unintentionally create monopolies

title: Re-evaluate baby formula regulations
proposal: The text recommends re-evaluating labeling and other rules that unnecessarily delay making and selling baby formula, citing recent shortages.
quote: labeling regulations and regulations that unnecessarily delay the manufacture and sale of baby formula should be re-evaluated

title: Stop grouping schools to qualify for free meals under CEP
proposal: The text recommends a USDA rule saying only a whole school or whole district, not a selected group of schools, can qualify for the Community Eligibility Provision.
quote: The USDA should issue a rule that clarifies that only an individual school or a school district as a whole, not a subset of schools within a district

title: Eliminate the Community Eligibility Provision for school meals
proposal: The text recommends that Congress end the Community Eligibility Provision, which lets all students in high-need schools get free meals.
quote: not become an entitlement for students from middle- and upper-income homes. Congress should eliminate CEP

title: Limit summer school meals to students in summer school
proposal: The text recommends that USDA not provide summer meals to students unless they are taking summer-school classes.
quote: the USDA should not provide meals to students during the summer unless students are taking summer-school classes

title: Reject universal free school meals
proposal: The text recommends returning school lunch and breakfast programs to serving only children in need and rejecting efforts to make free meals universal.
quote: Restore programs to their original intent and reject efforts to create universal free school meals.

title: Require measurable goals for farm conservation programs
proposal: The text recommends that conservation programs address real, current environmental problems with measurable goals, and pay farmers only for practices they would not have adopted anyway.
quote: As a general matter, the next Administration should ensure that these programs address genuine and specific environmental concerns

title: Eliminate the Conservation Reserve Program
proposal: The text recommends working with Congress to end the Conservation Reserve Program, which pays farmers not to farm some of their land.
quote: Champion the elimination of the Conservation Reserve Program. Farmers should not be paid in such a sweeping way not to farm their land.

title: Limit NRCS control over wetlands and erodible land on farms
proposal: The text recommends removing NRCS authority to prescribe specific practices on farms for program eligibility, using locally approved best-practice plans instead, and adding appeal protections for farmers.
quote: Problematic NRCS overreach could be avoided entirely by removing its authority to prescribe specific practices on a particular farm operation

title: Give states more power over wetlands and erodible land rules
proposal: The text recommends supporting legislation to shift more authority over erodible land and wetlands conservation to the states and possibly local conservation districts.
quote: At a minimum, a new Administration should support legislation to divest more power to the states (and possibly local SWCDs)

title: Stop USDA from creating new permanent conservation easements
proposal: The text recommends limiting permanent conservation easements and working with Congress to bar USDA from creating new ones.
quote: limit the use of permanent easements and collaborate with lawmakers to prohibit the USDA from creating new permanent easements

title: Allow state-inspected meat to be sold across state lines
proposal: The text recommends legislation to let meat and poultry from USDA-approved state-inspected plants be sold in interstate commerce.
quote: Promote legislation that would allow state-inspected meat to be sold in interstate commerce.

title: Reject new marketing orders and checkoff programs and end existing ones
proposal: The text recommends rejecting new marketing orders and checkoff programs where the law allows, ending existing ones when possible, easing termination, and opposing volume controls.
quote: The USDA should reject any new requests for marketing orders and checkoff programs to the extent authorized by law and eliminate existing programs when possible.

title: Eliminate marketing orders and checkoff programs by law
proposal: The text recommends working with Congress to eliminate marketing orders and checkoff programs entirely.
quote: Work with Congress to eliminate marketing orders and checkoff programs.

title: Require regular producer votes on checkoff programs
proposal: The text recommends legislation requiring those subject to checkoff programs and marketing orders to vote at least every five years on whether to continue them.
quote: For example, the voting should occur at least every five years, to determine whether a marketing order or checkoff program should continue.

title: Repeal the Market Access Program and other export promotion
proposal: The text recommends repealing market development programs like the Market Access Program and focusing the Foreign Agricultural Service on removing trade barriers.
quote: The USDA should work with Congress to repeal market development programs like the Market Access Program and similar programs.

title: Remove barriers to approving agricultural biotechnology
proposal: The text recommends that USDA counter what it calls scare tactics and adopt policies removing unnecessary barriers to approving and using biotechnology.
quote: adopt policies to remove unnecessary barriers to approvals and the adoption of biotechnology

title: Repeal the federal GMO food labeling law
proposal: The text recommends working with Congress to repeal the federal law requiring labels on genetically engineered food, while keeping federal preemption of state laws.
quote: The USDA should work with Congress to repeal the federal labeling law, while maintaining federal preemption

title: Fight foreign trade barriers to U.S. biotech crops
proposal: The text recommends USDA work with the U.S. Trade Representative to remove barriers other countries impose on U.S. biotech farm goods.
quote: The USDA should work closely with the Office of the United States Trade Representative to remove improper barriers imposed by other countries

title: Expand active forest management to reduce wildfires
proposal: The text recommends building on Executive Order 13855 and working with Congress to promote thinning and other active vegetation management and reduce regulatory obstacles to fuel reduction.
quote: This would involve embracing Executive Order 13855, building upon it, and working with lawmakers to promote active management of vegetation

title: Increase timber sales from national forests
proposal: The text recommends increasing timber sales in national forests, which it says would reduce the biomass that fuels wildfires.
quote: reduce regulatory obstacles to reducing fuel buildup, and increase timber sales

title: Repeal the federal Dietary Guidelines
proposal: The text recommends that USDA lead an effort with Congress to repeal the Dietary Guidelines for Americans.
quote: Work with lawmakers to repeal the Dietary Guidelines. The USDA should help lead an effort to repeal the Dietary Guidelines.

title: Keep Dietary Guidelines focused on nutrition, not the environment
proposal: At a minimum, the text recommends a more transparent Dietary Guidelines process that focuses only on nutrition, not issues like the environment, and writing these reforms into law.
quote: It should also ensure that the Dietary Guidelines focus on nutritional issues and do not veer off-mission by focusing on unrelated issues
